title: Something is random if essentially no simple program detects regularities in it

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Something is random if essentially no simple program detects regularities in it

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Since essentially all standard methods of perception and analysis are based on simple programs, something should be considered random whenever essentially no simple program succeeds in detecting regularities in it.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: something should be considered to be random whenever there is essentially no simple program that can succeed in detecting regularities in it.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Defining the Notion of Randomness” (from p. 552), p. 556. Scope: the definition of randomness for data of any kind

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-04: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Particular test suites can classify particular strings, but that would instantiate rather than test the definition. Competing definitions can agree on observations while differing conceptually.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: This is a proposed definition; without a fixed language, complexity bound, and quantifier replacing 'essentially no,' no observation can confirm that it is the correct meaning of randomness.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Normative definition rather than an empirical proposition.

Universal non-detection cannot be established by finite search.

Simple program is representation-dependent.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.15
operationalizability: 0.18
data adequacy: 0.1

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Wolfram is offering a definition: call something random when essentially no simple program detects regularities in it. That proposal can be adopted or rejected on grounds of usefulness, which is the subject of the surrounding argument, but no dataset confirms or refutes a stipulation. The empirical companion claim, about how rarely further programs succeed, is separate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The sentence proposes how the word 'random' should be used. Applying the proposed test to data illustrates the definition; it does not confirm or refute the recommendation to adopt it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A stipulative definition is not settled by the data it classifies.

'Essentially no simple program' is not itself a decidable property, so the definition does not yield a finite test.
